title: Microsoft Declares 'Code Red' After Historic Outage
description:
Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" initiative to overhaul its engineering and crisis response practices following a 24-hour outage on November 12-13 that disrupted governments, financial firms and airlines worldwide, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters. Never before had so many customers been without email for so long, said M365 Core President Jason Henderson. "Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team," Henderson added. From the report: Amanda Silver, Microsoft's corporate vice president overseeing M365 Core and Work IQ, the company's workplace intelligence platform for AI agents, said in a separate memo on Monday that engineers had to work through a "fog of war" as the outage unfolded. Despite deploying top engineering personnel, responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats and struggled to maintain a cohesive picture of hypotheses and decisions because diagnostic data was scattered across fragmented internal tracking systems, Silver said.
 
[...] As part of the Code Red, a high-priority mobilization reserved for critical crises, Silver outlined five workstreams focused on load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning and faster recovery mechanisms. Microsoft set a target of achieving worldwide resolution within an hour during future incidents and plans to deploy AI agents to help engineers diagnose system health data more quickly. Henderson said he would hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team, which oversees the engineering group responsible for underlying Microsoft 365 services, to track actions stemming from the outage, along with weekly reviews. The company spokesperson said Microsoft is committed not only to resolving issues when they occur, but to doing everything possible to prevent future disruptions.
 
"Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday," Henderson said, adding that he had conducted an extensive review of the broader organizational and structural issues that allowed the failures to occur. In another memo earlier this month reviewed by Reuters, Henderson said "urgent patches to our M365 Core services" took too long to deploy worldwide. "In a separate recent incident, an urgent production fix took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. For our most urgent security issues, we need to get from detection to safe worldwide deployment in an hour. Needless to say, we aren't here yet," he wrote.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

Kagi, the company behind the paid Google Search alternative and Orion web browser, has launched a public beta of Kagi Mail, an email service promising "no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in."
 
"Does the world need another email service? We asked ourselves that question more than once," Kagi says. "There are great ones out there, and we're fans of what Fastmail and Tuta are doing. We still built our own, for the same reason we build everything at Kagi: technology should do its job and then get out of your way." The Verge reports: With Kagi Mail, you get an @kagimail.com address, but the service also supports unlimited aliases and domains. It also offers 50GB of storage and a built-in calendar. On the roadmap, you can expect contacts and an address book in Q1 2027, but native mobile apps aren't expected to arrive until Q3 2027. Kagi Mail is available now with a 60-day free trial before you have to pay $99 per year. The service is available as part of a $25 per month Kagi Ultimate subscription.

title: Mayo Clinic To Give Appointment Workers 5 Paid Minutes a Day To Boot Up Computers
description:
Mayo Clinic has agreed to pay more than $906,000 in back wages to employees who schedule patient appointments. An investigation by Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison found that employees were performing unpaid work before and after their shifts, including time spent booting up computers and finishing patient calls. Under the settlement (PDF), Mayo will stop rounding employees' work hours and give them five paid minutes at the start of each shift to boot up their computers. CBS News reports: In a statement, Mayo Clinic said it reached the agreement to resolve concerns about "certain timekeeping practices" involving a group of the specialists. The clinic said it doesn't agree with the attorney general's position but decided that a resolution in which money went to its staff, rather than to defense fees, was preferable. Mayo said it is committed to paying employees accurately and appropriately and reviews its compensation policies regularly. Neither the announcement nor the statement says how many workers are covered or how far back the unpaid time goes.
 
"Under Minnesota law, workers need to be compensated for all the time they work," Ellison said. State law requires employers to pay employees for all time spent on duties connected to their jobs, including time on the employer's premises. Ellison said Mayo cooperated with the investigation and changed its policies on its own to pay workers for the time. He said other employers should take note: "they're on the clock and need to be paid" if they are on site or doing work duties. Ellison encouraged any worker who believes they're being underpaid to contact his office, saying it may be able to help co-workers as well.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: GTA 6 Hacker Released On License With Warning 'Don't Let This Happen Again'
description:
Arion Kurtaj, the 21-year-old Lapsus$ hacker responsible for the 2022 leak of Grand Theft Auto VI, was released on license the same day he was sentenced to seven years in prison. He is subject to a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order restricting his online activities, including banning him from Telegram and Discord. "You are a very talented young man," the judge told Kurtaj, warning him: "Don't let this happen again." The BBC reports: [...] With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj hacked Rockstar using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse. He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished GTA 6, which had been shrouded in secrecy until its release last week. He then broke into the company's internal Slack messaging system to declare: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code."
 
The company refused to co-operate so he posted the clips and source code on a forum under the username TeaPotUberHacker. Rockstar Games said it cost the firm $5 million to recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time. The company also said the breach revealed for the first time that one of the playable characters in the game was a woman -- a secret it was guarding closely for marketing purposes.

title: US To Blacklist Asian AI Firm Megaspeed After Nvidia Scandal
description:
The U.S. Commerce Department plans to blacklist Singapore-based AI infrastructure company Megaspeed and its subsidiary Speedmatrix over suspicions that they helped Chinese companies obtain restricted Nvidia AI chips. The move follows allegations that a former Megaspeed executive had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang while working as a Chinese intelligence asset, although Commerce officials say their investigation into the company began nearly two years ago. The BBC reports: The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US. The company is mainly a developer of data centers, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang. [...] When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed.
 
Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang. Alice Huang (no relation) was thought by US intelligence to be working as an asset for Beijing, creating national security concerns within the US. China has denied that she is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.

title: Russia May Launch Nuclear Weapon Into Orbit As Soon As Next Month
description:
Western intelligence agencies reportedly believe Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit as early as December, "suggesting the country's development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought," reports Ars Technica, citing German media reports. Such a launch would violate the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, while a detonation could create radiation belts that damage satellites for years. From the report: The orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia's own spacecraft and Chinese satellites.
 
Reporting from three German news outlets -- public broadcasters NDR and WDR and the Munich-based newspaper Suddeutsche Zeitung -- indicates Russia's launch of a nuclear-armed satellite could be imminent. The report says Western intelligence agencies, including the German Armed Forces and Federal Intelligence Service, believe Russia is preparing to deploy the weapon in space this year. Several NATO countries have exchanged their findings on the matter.
 
The nuclear-armed satellite, designated Sputnik-S, has been in storage in the greater Moscow area for years, the German news report said. German Space Command believes the satellite could be launched as early as December. Once in orbit, a nuclear weapon could loiter for months or years, ready for detonation on the command of Russian military forces. The Kremlin dismissed the report. "Given the number of qualifiers like 'allegedly' and 'possibly' -- not to mention the fact that the claims are attributed to some unspecified source -- they are hardly worth taking seriously," said Dmitry Peskov, spokesperson for Russian President Vladimir Putin.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

This specifically targets newer vehicles that may lock pre-installed features (like heated seats or screen compatibility) behind a paywall or subscription service. This is becoming more and more of a problem as years go by, and consumers have been very vocal against the practice, but this is a tangible step that can be taken to end this practice before it gets too out of hand. title: Google Is Finally Retiring the Nest App Early Next Year
description:
Google is shutting down its 15-year-old Nest app on January 25, 2027, requiring users to switch to Google Home to remotely control their smart home devices and receive notifications. "Then, on August 2, the company will retire Google Assistant on smart speakers and displays, with Gemini replacing the older tech for voice controls," reports Engadget. From the report: If you've yet to migrate your Nest devices to the Google Home app, the company says your existing settings and schedules will transfer over automatically. The only thing you need to manually move over are any custom clips you might have saved over the years. You can do this by visiting the Nest website before January 25 and clicking the "Download all" button. Google says it will automatically migrate Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions to its newer Google Home Premium package. "You will receive an email closer to the date of transfer detailing your subscription information," the company adds. "The Nest app launched over 15 years ago, and home technology has changed a lot since then," Google says of the decision. "To give every Nest user Google's latest security protections and most advanced cyber defenses, plus new features from Gemini, we're bringing all Nest devices together in the Google Home app."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Trump Halts Army's Plans to Detonate Bomb-Making Chemicals In Iowa
description:
President Trump has ordered the military to halt plans to detonate nearly five tons of unstable lead azide explosives at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. "Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa's governor-elect, who won't be sworn into office until January," reports Ars Technica. From the report: The Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP).
 
Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before planning the detonation.
 
Late Thursday, a federal appeals court granted Earthjustice's request to put a hold on the Army's permit from the Environmental Protection Agency, which allowed for the controlled detonation to be carried out. Around the same time, Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said the detonation would be postponed until Monday so the military could communicate with Iowans about the situation and plans.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: CrowdStrike to Buy Zscaler In $44 Billion Deal
description:
CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire network security provider Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal. "The deal marks CrowdStrike's biggest acquisition to date and is among the largest in the sector as businesses consolidate and ramp up defenses to fend off AI-powered attacks," reports CNBC. The acquisition is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028. From the report: "With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said in a statement. "We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen."
 
CrowdStrike has been a major beneficiary of skyrocketing demand for AI security, with shares soaring about 80% this year as of Monday's open. Zscaler shares are up about 5% year to date after Monday's surge. Their combined market value exceeded $265 billion as of Friday's close, behind market leader Palo Alto Networks at $282 billion.
 
[...] Analysts view the Zscaler deal as a major AI security opportunity, allowing CrowdStrike to capture more customer security spending and close a significant gap with Palo Alto. "The addition of ZS to CRWD's platform could bring more breadth in an era of vendor consolidation and, more importantly, network security to position the company more effectively for rising demand for AI Sovereignty," wrote analysts at JPMorgan.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Mesa 27.0 RadeonSI Gallium3D Disables Radeon Kernel Driver Support By Default
description: As part of encouraging AMD Radeon Linux users to switch over to the AMDGPU kernel driver and/or upgrade their kernels, Mesa 27.0 with the RadeonSI Gallium3D driver is disabling its Radeon kernel driver compatibility by default. This affects the early GCN 1.0 and GCN 1.1 graphics processors that had been still using the legacy Radeon kernel driver by default up until about a year ago when it reached feature parity on the AMDGPU kernel driver. For now the Radeon kernel driver support in Mesa 27.0 is disabled by default but can be re-enabled, but eventually that Radeon kernel driver support by RadeonSI will be removed...

title: Trump Is Said to Have Directed Effort to Reinstate Nvidia Chief
description:
President Trump reportedly directed a behind-the-scenes effort to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO, enlisting Vice President JD Vance to secure assurances from federal officials that Huang was not facing criminal charges or considered a national security risk. According to The New York Times, the intervention came despite intelligence concerns surrounding Huang's alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy linked to an investigation into illegal Nvidia chip shipments to China. From the report: [...] Only a tiny handful of officials at the highest level of the government were aware of these conversations. On Sunday night, Nvidia's board told the administration that it would be announcing Mr. Huang's reinstatement on Monday morning before the markets opened. The announcement included a note about a new compliance committee, intended to offer public assurance that the company was taking seriously the investigation into the possible smuggling of advanced chips. Mr. Trump was said to have been thrilled that the plan to restore Mr. Huang was executed without any leaks.
 
In directing Mr. Vance to engage with Mr. Huang and his peers, Mr. Trump was turning to one of the members of his administration with the strongest relationships in Silicon Valley. The vice president is close to some of Mr. Huang's biggest supporters and admirers, such as David Sacks, the investor and co-chairman of the President's Council of Advisers on Science and Technology. Mr. Sacks previously served as Mr. Trump's key adviser on artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency issues.
 
On Monday morning, Mr. Trump rejoiced in Nvidia's action, saying on his social media website Truth Social that the company "made the correct and proper decision." The president explicitly connected the reinstatement of Mr. Huang to the health of the U.S. economy. "The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy," Mr. Trump wrote.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: AMD EPYC Zen 6 vs. Zen 1 Performance: 12.1x Geo Mean In Less Than 10 Years, Up To 133x In AI
description: This month brought the availability of the new EPYC 9006 "Venice" SP7 Zen 6 server processors. We have seen excellent generational gains with the likes of the EPYC 9686F and EPYC 9996 over Zen 5 Turin CPUs as well as sharply outperforming the competition from Intel and NVIDIA. With the first-generation EPYC "Naples" processors having launched nearly ten years ago, I was curious to quantify AMD's server performance gains over the past decade. So up today is a look at how the EPYC 9996 and EPYC 9686F Zen 6 processors compare to the original EPYC Zen 1 flagship with the EPYC 7601 across real-world workloads for performance as well as power efficiency for some pretty epic gains.
